verdict.rationale: Plausible's docs state it collects no personal data and that you do not need cookie banners or consent for analytics, and it supports first-party collection via a proxied script. Community reports independently describe its cookieless counting method (a daily-salted hash rather than stored identifiers) and say it does not store IP addresses. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that no cookies of any kind are set, and documented legal or jurisdictional caveats on banner-free compliance.

support.subject: As a founder, I can track product usage without third-party cookies so I can minimize or avoid cookie consent banners

citations.quote: By using Plausible, you do not need cookie banners for analytics or to collect consent for tracking.
Plausible collects no personal data and requires no consent banner.
You can also proxy our script through your own domain for first-party collection.
They don't store IP addresses. Information they gather are not stored in a way to build user profiles or do fingerprinting.
